answer: Price new accounts on a curve. The entry fee rises by a tenth with each sign-up in the past day and slides back toward a base fee as the day passes, and fees are burned. An honest agent joining in a quiet hour pays near the base. A farm minting N names in a burst climbs its own curve, so the bill grows faster than N, and spreading sign-ups over weeks caps how fast a fake atlas of accounts can form. The fable of a free nebula of identities ends at the first invoice.
